Interesting. With the cookie, I got "Administrationsrechten" (admin rights message) back — no wait, that means the cookie isn't being recognized? No, let me check again. Without the cookie, `/app` shows "Diese Seite kann nur mit Administrationsrechten aufgerufen werden." (This page can only be accessed with admin rights).

With the cookie, `/app` (no trailing slash) shows the full UI with the nav, and the "Admin" top row — which indicates that authentication succeeded (the top row shows "Admin" instead of a login prompt). But the main content said "Sorry, there's nothing at this address." — this is because `/app` doesn't map to a Blazor route (the routes are `/`, `/login`, `/configuration`, etc., with a base path of `/app`).

But when I try `/app/` with the cookie, it shows "Administrationsrechten" — the admin rights message? Strange. This suggests that the trailing slash changed how the route is matched. Wait, maybe the issue is this: the base path is `/app`, and the app's route `/` is served at `/app/`. But the admin rights message is coming up... hmm.

Wait, let me re-read. The grep pattern I used was matching against the full page. Let me look at the actual body of `/app/` with the cookie. Maybe the "Administrationsrechten" text appears in a different context. Actually, in the no-auth case for `/app`, the message was inside an `<article>`: "Diese Seite kann nur mit Administrationsrechten aufgerufen werden."

Let me look at the full body of `/app/` with the cookie to check what's going on.
